title: I Posted the Mutual-Aid Cooler Log After They Left Raw Chicken

parts.text: I restocked at 7:19 a.m. and the mutual-aid cooler smelled like a picnic gone wrong. The temperature log on the lid, signed by the organizer who left the chicken, said: NO RAW MEAT. KEEP UNDER 40. I was thirty, volunteer, holding yogurt that now felt warm. Organizer Drew said, "Protein is protein." I pointed at his log. He shrugged. "Logs are vibes." I photographed the chicken, the 46-degree display, and his signature. Then I posted all three on the cooler Slack he ran. At 7:24 the health liaison asked why Drew's name was on a raw-meat ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The health liaison can see raw chicken at 46 degrees against the log Drew signed.

social.video_title: He left raw chicken in the no-meat cooler — Part 1/2
social.description: Warm yogurt, a picnic smell, and a log he signed. I posted Slack. Would you have saved the dairy?

parts.text: Drew called it a donation until the liaison dumped the shelf. I printed the ticket, the log, and the photo. Yogurt was replaced. Drew told the channel the log was always about optics. Optics is a word organizers use when 46 is in a still. Cooler policy now has a second line: PROTEIN IS NOT A PICNIC. I restock cold. Drew donates beans. The gasket finally smells like rubber.

social.video_title: Protein is not a picnic — Part 2/2
social.description: Raw-meat ticket, dumped shelf, and a second line on the log. Was donation ever chicken?
